loops.tagline: Series B AI infra — ship tickets, not whiteboard puzzles.

stages.title: CV submission
stages.summary: Talent profile + mission-fit narrative survives the 30-second scan.

stages.title: Technical foundations
stages.summary: Short async gate: rate limiting, APIs, and debugging instincts.

stages.title: Work Ticket
stages.summary: 4h scoped ticket in browser studio — AI allowed, prompts logged.

stages.title: Ethics & behavioral
stages.summary: Values + ownership under pushback — the round that decides the offer.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a rate limiter on a public API?
options: Encrypt traffic between clients and servers
Cap request volume per client to protect capacity and fairness
Cache responses to reduce database load
quizQuestions.explain: Rate limiters bound abuse and noisy neighbors — especially before beta traffic.

quizQuestions.prompt: A client receives HTTP 429. What should the response include?
options: Retry-After (or equivalent) so clients know when to retry
A redirect to the marketing site
quizQuestions.explain: Well-behaved clients need a time hint — standard for token-bucket APIs.

quizQuestions.prompt: Token bucket vs fixed window — which is usually smoother for bursts?
options: Token bucket allows controlled bursts within the refill rate
quizQuestions.explain: Token buckets are the usual choice for per-IP API limits.

quizQuestions.prompt: You flip a fair coin until you get heads. Expected number of flips?
Look-ahead bias in a backtest usually means…
options: Using future information when making past decisions
Running the backtest on too little data
quizQuestions.explain: Future data leaking into features or labels invalidates the simulation.

quizQuestions.prompt: A report with 200 charts for a trading prompt most likely signals…
options: You don't know what matters yet
quizQuestions.explain: Brevity + decisive views beat chart dumps in quant research screens.
